what_it_is: The persistent state of the work - what survives between runs. Not the run's sign-out (that's the act of passing). Carry is the standing top-10 list per area, the unresolved items with their context, the blockers with their owners. The worker rotates every wave; the list does not.
what_it_does: Answers the successor's first question - 'where do I start?' - before she asks it. And answers the machine's question: gap-recycling. An unresolved item doesn't get dropped or re-derived from scratch - it returns to the queue with its full context intact.
why_it_matters: Without carry, every wave starts cold: the new worker re-reads everything, gaps die in local notes. Paid for twice: stale carries outliving their resolution (a 'still pending' carried forward after the resolution already landed - the list lying to its reader), and waves starting cold with no standing list. A carry list that lies is worse than no list.
key_rules: Keep a standing ranked top-10 list per area: living, current, ranked by what blocks success most. Lives in the run's venue sign-out (REMAINING section - the freshest copy), the queue it feeds (the durable copy), and the area's own standing list. The successor reads the sign-out first, the queue second - she continues from the list, never rebuilds it.
Every carry line names its last-verified timestamp. A line without a timestamp is a rumor, not a carry.

A carried 'still pending' is a claim - re-verify it at carry time: check against the newest sibling receipts before carrying forward. When two receipts disagree, the live byte-check decides - route to bytes before routing to a judge (L401). Carry nothing you haven't re-checked.
Gap-recycling: unresolved items return to the queue with their context - what was tried, what failed, who owns the unblock. The next run starts at the gap, not at zero.
Never hand-carry a cached copy across runs: re-derive state at run start. A stale torch is worse than none.
Drop what's resolved, and note the resolution: carrying a closed item forward is the stale-carry defect.

not_covered: The run transition itself - the act of passing (COMPLETED / REMAINING / RECOMMEND NEXT + explicit tag-off)
The accountability loop - who's working, the ghost rule, the read receipt

mechanically_enforced: The briefing's 14-question orientation: 'WHAT happened previously? Read the venue tail and the learning log' - the carry list is the entry gate of every run.
The claim-liveness audit (L399): ghost claims are recycled back to the queue automatically.
The sign-out procedure (COMPLETED / REMAINING / RECOMMEND NEXT) is the carry list's authoring format.
proposed: A machine check that diffs carry lines against newest receipts before accepting them. Does not exist - the re-verification-at-carry-time rule is a norm, enforced by reviewers and the L401 precedent, not by code.

self_test: Does every 'still pending' on my carry list name its last-verified timestamp?
Could a cold successor start from my list alone - no questions, no re-derivation?
Did I re-verify each carry line against the newest receipts before carrying it forward?
